newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asia stocks fall on lower Dow, Nikko forecast.
newsitem.headline: Asia stocks fall on lower Dow, Nikko forecast.

text.p: Most Asia stock markets were lower on Friday after a volatile performance on Wall Street overnight, where early gains evaporated and left the market down more than 90 points on record volume.
Tokyo shares also weakened on a rise in the dollar/yen to a near four-year high overnight and an unfavourable profit warning by Japan's third largest securities house.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 94.28 points, or 1.38 percent, at 6,755.75 on Thursday after rising above 6,900 for the first time.
Record volume of 683 million shares exceeded the previous record of 680 million on July 16, 1996.
The sudden turnaround was the direct product of a rapid sequence of sell programs apparently triggered by developments in the futures market.

Just as the Dow was surpassing the 6900 mark for the first time in its history, the futures contract on the Standard & Poor's 500 index was also nearing a key psychological level, said Mike Rothberg, managing director of portfolio trading at Cantor Fitzgerald.
On Friday, the Tokyo market remained edgy over the yen's performance and the implications it could have for an already uncertain economic outlook.
The dollar was trading around 119.20 yen at midday, after falling to around 118.70 earlier in the session.
It had hit a 47-month high of 119.80 yen overnight in New York, but its rise was kept in check by sales of dollar's for yen by the Bank of Tokyo and other central banks, dealers said.
Problems surrounding Japanese banks and financial companies also weighed on the stock market, dealers said.

Comments that Nikko Securities Co Ltd, Japan's third largest brokerage house, may not reach the company's projected earnings for the year ended March 31, 1997 because of the fall in the Japanese market cast a pall over the market. "We cannot be optimistic (about the target)",Masao Yuki, Nikko's executive vice president told Reuters in an interview.
These factors served as a backdrop to two separate major deals involving Sony Corp and Sega Enterprises Ltd aimed at strengthening their positions in different segments of the entertainment field.

Sony gained 30 yen to 7,750 on reports it struck a deal with Rupert Murdoch's News Corp for a satellite broadcasting venture, while Sega was off 200 yen at 3,460 after Thursday's news of its merger with toy maker Bandai Co Ltd.
As of 0600 GMT the Nikkei 225 index was off 260.10 points, or 1.23 percent, at 17,689.36.
In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index lost 176.41 points, or 1.30 percent, by midday, to 13,433.92, after the selloff in the Dow triggered a drop in the Hang Seng index futures market.
"We saw a bit of panic selling at the open, but the cash market has pulled us up," said one Hang Seng futures trader.
Shares in Hongkong Electric Co Ltd fell HK$0.25 to HK$26.75 in morning trade, but the downside was capped after a report said an offer for the company by Hutchinson Whampoa Ltd was undervalued.
Taiwan and Malaysian shares bucked the downward trend and posted modest gains.

Taiwan's weighted index closed up 28.46 points, or 0.39 percent, at 7,313.08 on bargain hunting after Thursday's selloff, dealers said, while Malaysia's benchmark Composite index gained 2.20 points, or 0.18 percent, to 1,244.07.
In the Philippines, Ayala Corp's shares rose sharply after a winning bid to privatise the Manila waterworks.
The main index closed up 4.15 points, or 0.12 percent, at 3,332.53 points. Ayala B shares gained 1.50 pesos, or 5.26 percent, to 30 pesos.

Elsewhere in Asia, Indonesian shares lost 4.759 points, or 0.69 percent, to 680.22 in early trade, while Thai stocks recouped losses to eak out a 0.78 point gain to 849.95. Singapore's Straits Times Index slid 7.53 points, or 0.33 percent, to 2,240.81, while Korean shares fell on concern over Thursday's news Hanbo Steel Corp had defaulted on its debts.
At the midday break Korean shares were off 4.87 points, or 0.72 percent, to 672.04.
Australia's All Ordinaries Index ended down 11.50 points, or 0.47 percent, at 2,423.0, while New Zealand shares shed 17.53 points, or 0.73 percent, to 2,400.27.
